contracts.title: 2027-09 Strategic assessment of forestry operations in NSW
contracts.scope: The Service Provider will support the NSW Governments strategic assessment process by undertaking ecological field surveys, data management, analysis and reporting to validate State Vegetation Type Mapping (SVTM) and assess vegetation condition across Regional Forest Agreement (RFA) subregions in New South Wales. The services comprise three phases: Phase 1 – Survey planning and logistics: Development of survey methodologies, planning of field activities, management of work health and safety requirements, land access arrangements, site identification and data collection protocols. Phase 2 – Field surveys, analysis and reporting: Delivery of vegetation integrity and rapid flora surveys by suitably qualified personnel; collection and management of field data; spatial and ecological analysis; validation and refinement of vegetation mapping; assessment of vegetation condition; and preparation of technical reports and datasets. Phase 3 – Response to feedback: Revision of reports and supporting information in response to stakeholder feedback on the Draft Strategic Assessment, including additional field surveys where required. The services also include documentation of evidence, assumptions and limitations; provision of project data and deliverables in editable electronic formats; and transfer of intellectual property and associated usage rights to the NSW Government in accordance with contractual requirements.

contracts.title: DOE08471/25 - VET Teacher Training Provider Panel (Refresh)
contracts.scope: The Department has oversight of the Vocational Education and Training (VET) Teacher Training Program. This program is managed on behalf of and in cooperation with other school sectors - Catholic Schools NSW (CSNSW) on behalf of diocesan RTOs and the Independent Schools of NSW (ISNSW) on behalf of the Registered Training Organisations (RTO) in the Independent School sector. The Department coordinates approved training through the VET Teacher Training Program for teachers to deliver VET courses to secondary students in NSW schools. In 2025, the Department established a panel of providers for VET Training Programs for Secondary School Teachers consisting of 11 contractors. The current arrangement commenced on 1 February 2025 and expires on 31 January 2028. There are also two by one year extension options at the discretion of the Department, potentially taking the contract term out to 31 January 2030. The Department’s annual review of the training programs provided under the program and the existing provider panel showed gaps in coverage, making a panel refresh necessary. Refer to the tender documentation for details.

contracts.scope: The southern section of Mundowy Lane will be upgraded to a level preventing inundation during flows up to 45,000 ML/day at Wagga Wagga. This will allow the passage of higher flows through the culverts, reducing the risk of damage to the road and mitigating impacts to adjacent properties. Specific activities include: undertaking geotechnical investigations conducting topographical and property boundary surveys reviewing environmental factors, including conducting biodiversity and cultural heritage assess completing detailed designs and procuring a construction contractor constructing the new infrastructure, commissioning and handing over to the asset owner engaging with stakeholders and working with landholders where land may need to be accessed for temporary construction works, if required.

contracts.agency: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development
contracts.title: Slickline Services - Stage 2B Project
contracts.supplier: KINETIC WELL INTERVENTION SERVICES PTY LTD
contracts.scope: The rig-based completion program is expected to commence from March 2026 (exact timing to be confirmed pending availability of workover rig). The two-well completions program is estimated to take approximately 22 days in total for the campaign, with six (6) days per well and allowing for one inter-well move and initial campaign mobilisation and end of campaign demobilisation, which may require slickline services assistance to deploy/retrieve downhole slickline plug for packer setting and/or packer pressure testing. Once completions have been installed, a well test equipment package will be mobilised once workover rig is moved off well location and each well will be flow tested consecutively over April to June 2026. The well test approach will utilise an ESP to flow water to surface while monitoring of pressures and flow rates to establish reservoir characteristics (assuming no gas or hydrocarbons are present in the well stream). It is anticipated that each zone in the well may be selectively flow tested for up to 10 days each with an overall well test duration on each well of approximately ~30 days per well. Slickline services will be required throughout the well testing duration to open and/or close SSDs accordingly as required to flow test each zone of interest. Supplier is to provide all equipment, materials and personnel for the provision of services required to complete the wells with a design and operational plan as detailed in the Technical Scope.

contracts.title: C_2621436: Native Ground Cover Direct Seeding
contracts.scope: GS LLS has carried out soil remediation across 35 hectares of degraded grassland within the DEOH. This work targeted both the physical and chemical properties of the soil (Refer to figure 1 for direct seeding mapping). The soil remediation addressed several known soil issues, including low carbon levels, low pH, reduced calcium, elevated magnesium and manganese and poor soil structure through various soil remediation actions and ameliorants. Following the completion of the soil remediation the 35 hectares was seeded with a sterile cover crop (rye corn) to protect the topsoil from erosion and weed invasion. The site will be ready for direct seeding with native groundcovers (this contract) before Spring 2026.

contracts.title: LALC Aboriginal Employment Program
contracts.scope: The delivery partner will provide end‑to‑end program delivery services to support the Aboriginal Employment Program. This includes undertaking respectful engagement with Local Aboriginal Land Councils (LALCs) to understand local priorities, strengths, employment aspirations and capacity needs. The partner will assess community capability to identify opportunities, barriers and tailored support requirements The provider will co‑design culturally grounded employment pathways with each participating LALC, ensuring alignment with community context, cultural authority and local decision‑making. They will work alongside NSWALC, LLS and LALCs to support recruitment, onboarding, mentoring, governance strengthening, and training linked to land management, cultural practice and caring for Country The scope also includes supporting program implementation through a partnership model, coordinating delivery activities, facilitating cultural and community engagement, and documenting progress, learnings and shared reflections to enable continuous improvement. The provider must ensure cultural integrity, safety and respect throughout delivery, and maintain flexible, community‑led methods that adapt to emerging needs.

contracts.title: Salesforce Managed Support Services
contracts.scope: The scope of services includes delivery of an end‑to‑end Salesforce managed service supporting the Department’s CMS, IR, and ORALRA applications. Services cover day‑to‑day administration, including user management, configuration, data integrity, and environment management to maintain secure, stable, and efficient operations. Development services include the design, build, and deployment of enhancements, new functionality, and integrations aligned to business and technology priorities. Supervised issue investigation, root‑cause analysis, and solution delivery will be undertaken in collaboration with departmental teams. Incident management services include resolution of issues in accordance with agreed SLAs, with escalation to Salesforce or third‑party vendors where required. Structured change and release management processes will be applied to all changes, including impact assessment, testing in non‑production environments, and deployment through established governance processes. Ongoing services include proactive monitoring, health checks, risk and impact assessments, and continuous improvement activities. Regular reporting will be provided covering system performance, incidents, enhancements, security and compliance, service levels, and financial matters. Training, documentation, and knowledge transfer activities are included to support internal capability uplift and maximise the value of the Department’s Salesforce platforms.

contracts.title: Precinct Plans for Flood Impacted Areas of Lismore
contracts.scope: The overall objective of this project is to develop precinct plans to set out the most appropriate long term land use, ownership and ongoing management for land that has been bought back under the Resilient Homes Program within each of the four precincts and then prepare a Planning Proposal to appropriately rezone the land. Concurrently, an ownership and management strategy will need to be developed to inform decisions and future ownership of the land. The Planning Proposal will be reliant on inputs from the master planning and urban design exercise and will draw on the community and stakeholder engagement undertaken through the process, with a focus on implementation. The future use of land will respond to complex flood risk, and a range of technical inputs covering land contamination, a land use needs analysis, changing infrastructure needs, economic, social, environmental and cultural analysis to inform decisions to create a more sustainable and resilient Lismore. The outcomes will result in substantial changes to Lismore, with significant areas of previously residential land being converted to other land uses and zones. The Lismore community is still recovering from the 2022 floods, and this project is an opportunity to develop a positive vision for the future through meaningful collaboration with the community and other stakeholders.

contracts.title: SINSW07601/25 - Spring Farm Public School - Architectural Services - Phase 2 - Optional Phases 3-6
contracts.scope: Spring Farm Public School is situated at 26-36 Springs Road, Spring Farm, NSW 2570. The school is situated within the Camden Primary School Community Group (SCG), within the city of Camden Council Local Government Area (LGA).Currently, the existing site accommodates 22 permanent teaching spaces and 17 demountable teaching spaces.Due to overcrowding issues at Spring Farm Public School, the site will undergo an upgrade to provide additional teaching spaces to meet current and future demand within the schools catchment.The master planning scope of the project includes the upgrade of the school to an EFSG large primary school with a total of 48 permanent teaching spaces (including 4 support teaching spaces), and other upgrades to existing teaching spaces, core facilities and amenities. The additional teaching spaces will be accommodated in a new (up to) 4 storey building. A new large Hall, canteen and out-of-school hours (OOSH) care facility will be provided. The works at Griffith will involve interface with the existing hospital redevelopment, including coordination of demolition of carparks, installation of stormwater infrastructure and significant landscaping. contracts.title: Sunny Corner Mine Remediation Detailed Design Consultancy
contracts.scope: The design consultant is to undertake the following services: 1. Undertake a desktop review of background documentation to inform the detailed design. 2. Undertake initial site inspection to assess site conditions. 3. Undertake a review of subsidence hazards at the Sunny Corner Mine site that may impact the proposed remediation works. 4. Prepare a Design Options Report for the works including preparation of at least two (2) concept design options. 5. Undertake a detail survey of the site to inform the detailed design. 6. Undertake geotechnical investigations including non-intrusive methods such as geophysical survey and ground penetrating radar (GPR). 7. Undertake soil sampling and testing (geotechnical and geochemical) of the nominated stockpiled borrow material from the Bobs Creek Quarry. 8. Prepare a Geotechnical Investigation Report that details the methodology, test results and findings from the geotechnical site investigations. 9. Undertake design development of remediation works to inform the development of a detailed design that is construct only except for the Southern waste rock cut quantities and fill for the open pits. 10. Prepare draft detailed design documentation drawings for a construct only contract. 11. Prepare Final Detailed Design Documentation of the preferred remediation option. 12. Prepare Issued For Construction (IFC) documentation of the preferred remediation option.

contracts.title: SINSW-25-32246 - Nyngan Public School - New Playground
contracts.scope: The Contractor shall be responsible for the complete design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of a new playground facility. contracts.title: AHO– Primary Design Services – WYONG
contracts.scope: The AHO requires primary design services (head architect and subcontractors) to complete the design services package to deliver a residential flat building of 22-25 units, comprising a mix of two and one bedroom configurations (1x2B and 1x1B) with associated carparking at 8 Hargrave Street, Wyong The dwellings are to comply with AHO Design guidelines, AHO Fixtures Finishes Equipment (FFE) Schedule, AHO Components schedule (Solar and Airconditioning) and the Silver level of the Liveable Housing Design guidelines. The deliverables are to include concept design, design development, approvals, tender and construction documentation for the development.

All three FCVs are ideally to be completed and delivered by the end of June 2026, as per this RFQ and the Standing Offer Head Agreement, unless unforeseen circumstances necessitate an alternative arrangement. Briefing: The NSW SES invites panel members to attend a two part briefing to be held at 10am on 1st July 2025 at NSW SES Operational Support Unit - 1 Drummond St, Coniston, NSW.  Part 1: Briefing will be an recorded online and in-person presentation overviewing SESs current FCV including use cases for operations and future plans and ideas for Gen 2. Part 2: In-person guided tour of the current FCV to allow panel members access to have a closer look and ask questions of the current and future FCV.  Briefing is not mandatory. NOTE: Current FCV may be recalled to operations, in this situation the in-person briefing will not go ahead. Confirmation of briefing will be sent Thurs/Fri the week prior and a register of interest to attend will be sent out prior reconfirming date and time.

contracts.title: SWMHIP PCLI -Stage 2 - BCA and PCA Services
contracts.supplier: The Trustee for Blackett Family Trust & The Trustee for Heaslip Family Trust & The Trustee for THE GOLDSMITH FAMILY TRUST & The Trustee for The Maguire Family Trust
contracts.scope: The core project scope of PCLI Stage 2 includes: § Delivery of 60 residential units (targeting 6 sites) across three Local Health Districts (LHD) § Integration of clinical, housing, and operational inputs into a single documentation package § Management of site-specific planning pathways, being REF approvals § Preparation of fully certified (Design and Building Practitioners Act) design documentation § Application of the FDB, PPR, Mental Health FFE Guidelines, and DGNs § Collaboration across HI, MHB, LHDs, and NGO service providers § Each facility will support approximately 10 single-bed units with staff and communal areas, delivered under Class 3 provisions and subject to the Design and Building Practitioners Act 2020. Provide BCA and PCA services for six PCLI Stage 2 sites across HNELHD, NSLHD and WSLHD. For the BCA scope, provide compliance advice across all project stages, review designs for BCA, DDA and Access standards, certifying plans, liaise with consultants, and deliver compliance reports to support approvals. For the PCA scope, ensure compliance with NCC and REF, validate fire and design requirements, and certify statutory approvals, supported by specialist consultant inputs.

contracts.agency: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development
contracts.title: Workover rig, camp and support
contracts.supplier: THE TRUSTEE FOR WILD DESERT UNIT TRUST
contracts.scope: Proposals to commence the work at any time from 1 October 2025 until 30 April 2026 will be accepted. Both 12-hour and 24-hour operations will be considered. Final program scope is to be finalised, so there are three operational scenarios that may eventuate and Suppliers should factor into their commercial proposals as relevant. The completions program involves running completions to depths of 790 m to 2,000 m. The work is estimated to take approximately 28 days total for all three wells to be completed. This comprises 7 days per well operations time, time for two inter-well moves, initial campaign mobilisation and end of campaign demobilisation. Please note that this 28-day campaign assumes 24-hour operations and will be longer in the case of 12-hour operations. The total campaign length will also depend on the number of wells in which completions are installed. Supplier is to provide all equipment, materials and personnel for the provision of Workover Rig Services required to complete the wells with a design and operational plan as detailed in the Technical Scope. A mini camp (offices for rig and servcies crew, smoko/break shed and toilet facilities) on location must also be included as a part of the rig. The supplier is invited to provide a fully equipped main camp to accommodate rig and camp crew and up to fifteen (15) third-party personnel. Optionally, the supplier may also provide quotationfor the provision of cementing, slickline and tubular running/installation services.

contracts.title: TELCO/TEL-17732 Procurement of Professional Services for Network As Built documentations
contracts.scope: NSWTA requires the development of comprehensive as-built documentation to accurately capture thecurrent state of the RADNET network environments. This documentation is critical to providing a clear andauthoritative baseline of the existing physical and logical architectures, including configurations,interdependencies, and operational procedures. Establishing this baseline will reduce the risk ofmisalignment, support effective environment management, and enable a smoother integration phase tomeet current and future service level agreements (SLAs).The engagement will also deliver a structured gap analysis, undertaken in consultation with NSWTAstakeholders, to identify and remediate discrepancies between existing documentation and the live networkenvironment across each data centre. The scope of work will focus on four key operational locations: CastleHill Data Centre and National Operations Centre, Silverwater Data Centre, Unanderra Data Centre, and theSydney Olympic Park National Operations Centre.

contracts.title: Energy Efficiency Program FY25/26: Solar Supply
contracts.scope: The AHO is seeking tenders for the supply of solar panels and inverters (Goods) that meet the AHOs’ technical requirements as described in the Scope of Work. The Tenderers must supply and store the solar panels and inverters for collection by the AHO Installers. Tenderers will be responsible for the Goods until collection and transfer of Title to the AHO Contract Installers. This transfer will include all responsibility apart from the manufacturer’s warranty (the tenderer will be held responsible warranty and replacement parts). This program will require the supply of up to 224 5kW Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems including panels and inverters (installed by AHO contractors) by 30 June 2026. However, the Contract term will be for a full twelve months to accommodate any installation delays arising from tenant access or related issues. During this period, the supplier must have the capability to securely store the solar PV systems until such time as the AHO Installer is able to complete installation.

contracts.scope: The AHO is seeking tenders for the installation of solar panels and inverters (Goods) that meet the AHOs technical requirements as described in Attachment 4 – Scope of Work – Energy Efficiency FY26 – Solar Install. The Tenderers must collect and install the solar panels and inverters from the AHO Contract Suppliers. Tenderers will be responsible for the Goods from collection and transfer of Title from the AHO Contract Suppliers until transfer of Title to the AHO. This transfer will include all responsibility apart from the manufacturer’s warranty. This program for works is based on the installation of 224 5kW Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Systems on AHO properties, with the contractor aiming to complete all installations prior to 30 June 2026. The Contract term will be for a full twelve (12) months to accommodate any delays arising from tenant access or related issues.

contracts.scope: The Family and Injured Workers Support and Advisory Group (FIWSAG) is a SafeWork NSW constituted and supported group of individuals affected by a workplace incident involving a death, serious injury or illness. The members draw on their lived experience of serious workplace incidents to provide advice to SafeWork NSW about the information and support needs of persons affected by serious workplace incidents to help improve service delivery. Members also advocate for work health and safety in the community and provide support to others in similar circumstances. Clinical psychological support is provided to the FIWSAG to ensure the ongoing psychological safety of all group members and other participants at meetings and events where FIWSAG members are present and/or members stories are shared. Support is delivered via a specialised service model that includes psychological support, counselling, and clinical interventions by an appropriately qualified psychologist, as well as wellbeing support training for members to enable them to provide compassionate support to others in similar circumstances.

contracts.title: Manning Base Hospital - CSB Chiller Replacement Project
contracts.scope: This project involves the replacement of existing chillers and associated systems within the Clinical Services Building at Manning Base Hospital, with a primary focus on maintaining uninterrupted hospital operations and ensuring safety throughout delivery. Works include the procurement and installation of new chillers and associated pipework to improve system The scope also covers high-risk work management, particularly crane operations required for lifting and positioning heavy equipment. Comprehensive lift planning, risk assessments, and certified procedures will be implemented in compliance with NSW SafeWork guidelines. Commissioning will ensure at least one chiller remains operational at all times to support critical hospital services. Upon completion, the contractor will provide as-built documentation, operation manuals, and maintenance schedules, along with training for hospital staff. All works will adhere to MW21 Conditions of Contract, relevant Australian Standards, and hospital-specific requirements for safety, infection control, and emergency access.

contracts.title: Canterbury Hospital Redevelopment - Cost Manager (Parts 4 to 9)
contracts.scope: The Canterbury Hospital Redevelopment seeks to engage a specialist Cost Manager to provide expert cost management services throughout the planning, design, procurement, and construction phases of the project. Option – extending the number of participating businesses to 30 and the forming of a 3rd benchmarking group.

contracts.title: insw_2400325
contracts.scope: A multi-stage competitive procurement process was undertaken for this project. The first stage was an Expression of Interest (EOI), through which comprehensive market sounding and testing activities were conducted. Following this process, four proponents were invited to participate in the second stage - a Limited Request for Tender (RFT) process. The objective of this procurement was to engage a suitably experienced head contractor for the design finalization and construction of Bank Street Park. The RFT was issued to the four shortlisted tenderers on February 28, 2025, and the closing date was extended twice, resulting in a final closing time of 3:00 pm on May 22, 2025. The RFT remained open to the market for a total period of 11 weeks and 6 days. The evaluation was conducted in accordance with the pre-approved Tender Evaluation Plan (TEP), which, among other matters, outlined the governance arrangements, evaluation criteria, and weightings. The TEP was endorsed by all Evaluation Committee members, as well as the Project Review Committee (PRC) and the Procurement and Probity Advisors.

This forms a pilot program with potential for more sites in the future. Currently, most of these communities have no mobile or internet coverage. The Wi-Fi and VOIP systems can be connected by satellite backhaul or other similar innovative technology. This can be via a combination of terrestrial and celestial equipment to provide digital connectivity services to residential premises that are fitted with small antennas to collect and retransmit the digital signals. contracts.agency: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development
contracts.title: Carrai/Werrikimbe Disaster Recovery Funding Agreement (DRFA) – Stage 2
contracts.scope: The works include re-sheeting sections of 70km Trail within the Carrai, Willi Willi and Werrikimbe National Parks and in particular Coachwood and Carrai Roads. Gravel sheeting is required to improve traction and reduce slippage, after reshaping the carriageway surface. This process involves adding a layer of gravel, typically around 150mm thick, to the existing surface to create a more stable and less slippery riding surface. Gravel re-sheeting typically involves loosening the existing surface (e.g., with a tyning machine) to ensure proper bonding with the new gravel layer. A layer of new gravel is then spread evenly across the surface. Finally, the gravel is compacted to create a solid, stable surface. The works may also include clearing regrowth and vegetation, repairing trail surfaces, clearing drainage structures and culvert cleaning and repairs. This engagement will involve the provision of various plant and equipment items, each with qualified operators, under a wet hire arrangement. The equipment required includes: • D4/D5 Bulldozer with 6-way PAT blade • Grader • Roller • Water Cart • Rigid Truck • Posi Track • Moxy 30T Articulated Dump Truck • 1.7 Tonne Excavator • 14 Tonne Excavator Note: Plant may be required intermittently across different stages and must be available on an as-needed basis to meet program timelines.

contracts.title: Farms of the Future Mobile Learning Centre
contracts.scope: Project Timeline The Mobile Learning Centre should be operationally ready for deployment by mid-September 2025. Suppliers should provide a project schedule. Timely delivery is critical. Operating Outcomes The Mobile Learning Centre must deliver a high-quality, engaging educational experience focused on agricultural technology. It must include Virtual Reality (VR) and/or Augmented Reality (AR) experiences as well as interactive learning stations showcasing technologies such as sensors and data platforms. Facilitation space for workshops, demonstrations, and presentations both inside and outside of the Centre should be considered. The Mobile Learning Centre must be accessible, climate-controlled, and suitable for deployment in regional and rural environments. Technical Outcomes The vehicle must be equipped with reliable power supply systems, connectivity infrastructure to support digital content delivery and secure storage for equipment and educational materials. All technology must be user-friendly, durable, and supported by appropriate training and documentation. It is expected that the development of content and resources will be completed in collaboration with the Farms of the Future program. Some existing education materials have been developed and are available through an online Learning Management System, however the development of innovative VR experiences and content as part of this EOI will be considered. The Mobile Learning Centre will be operated from Sept 25 to Dec 27.

contracts.title: Notopala sublineata sublineata translocation and captive care
contracts.supplier: The Trustee for THE BROOKS FAMILY TRUST
contracts.scope: Translocation and Captive Care of rock and Notopala sublineata sublineata. Any collection and care of the snail will have to be undertaken in accordance with the conditions of the Section37 permit (Fisheries Management Act 1994). The Notopala sublineata sublineata snail is listed as a Critically endangered species under the NSW Fisheries Management Act 1994 (FM Act). While undertaking a site survey for the Aquatic Impact Assessment for the Louth Weir Fishway Review of Environmental Factors live snails were found. Following this a section 37 permit under the FM Act was obtained to do further surveys of live snails at Louth and Tilpa Weirs. During this survey populations of live snails were recorded at both Louth and Tilpa. It was determined that the Proposed Northern Basin Toolkit – Fish Passage project at Louth will have a significant impact on the snail. Service Include Generate and maintain an acceptable snail environment (biofilm)Import rock and Notopala sublineata sublineata snail into QLD from an agreed handover point located at Louth WeirUndertake captive breeding proof of concept with 10-15 snails collected from Louth Weir. Risk management measures are to be identified to maintain and breed the snailsCollaborate with Narrandera captive breeding proof of conceptDeliver a proof-of-concept report (inc husbandry assessment and nutritional requirements)

contracts.title: Pathways to Community Living (PCLI) Stage 2 - Capital Consultants - Cost Manager
contracts.scope: PCLI Stage 2 will deliver up to six separate supported housing facilities, each containing 10-20 single bedroom units which include facilities for independent daily living such as kitchen and laundry. Each facility will include staff support areas and shared communal spaces. The PCLI facilities will be single or two storey buildings of high quality residential nature and robust design. The buildings will be located within low/medium density residential areas or areas that are residential in character, to support community connection. PCLI facilities are not typical healthcare facilities and NSW Health has developed a draft Functional Design Brief to guide the design of PCLI facilities, which considers the specific requirements of PCLI consumers. These PCLI facilities will be delivered across up to six different sites. Two of these sites have been confirmed, two additional sites have been identified but not yet confirmed via Health governance, and two further sites have not yet been identified. The project comprises the core scope and two exercisable options: · Core scope: 20 PCLI beds across up to 2 sites · Option A: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option B: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option C: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option D: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site.

contracts.title: First Nations Remote Community Wi-Fi Connectivity
contracts.scope: Regional Digital Connectivity is seeking to procure free community Wi-Fi and VOIP services for selected First Nations communities. The Department’s Aboriginal Outcomes team has been consulted and have selected First Nations target communities to be provided with the Wi-Fi and VOIP services. This forms a pilot program with potential for more sites in the future. Currently, most of these communities have no mobile or internet coverage. The Wi-Fi and VOIP systems can be connected by satellite backhaul or other similar innovative technology. This can be via a combination of terrestrial and celestial equipment to provide digital connectivity services to residential premises that are fitted with small antennas to collect and retransmit the digital signals. Each location will have slightly different deliverable scopes based on consultations conducted in community by the Aboriginal Outcomes team. A detailed technical specifications sheet will be provided under a non-disclosure agreement once the applicant has submitted a complying Part B1 response form.

contracts.title: Rail control system - Parramatta Linen Service
contracts.scope: The scope is fully outlined in attached specifications document, the work includes upgrading control systems for the Classified Sorting Rail System, the Small Clean 50Kg Rail System, and the Large Clean 100Kg Rail System. This includes replacing and upgrading control cabinets, PLC components, power supplies, processors, communication modules, and input/output modules. The supplier must upgrade PLC control for all sorting bins and implement an override system to allow the sorting belt to operate independently of rail issues. The supplier must supply, install, wire, and connect control cabinets and servers, including any additional necessary cabling, and provide four PCs to enable users to view all three systems via a single interface. The supplier must ensure compliance with NSW Health’s Security Policy Requirements, collaborate with HealthShare ICT for integration, and provide network architecture diagrams. Additional UPS units should be supplied if needed. Finally, training for PLS maintenance staff on system operation and maintenance is required.

contracts.title: LAHC 2024/309 Modern Methods of Construction Research and Development - BH2V9
contracts.scope: Homes NSW has partnered with the BUILDING 4.0 CRC LIMITED to undertake research, development and delivery of Modern Methods of Construction program. The purpose of the program is to undertake research on best practice, analyse Homes NSW portfolio, product and processes to develop an operational model to scale the delivery of Modern Methods of Construction. Phase 1 – Scoping, strategy and development (complete) The first phase of the project was focused on scoping, strategy and development. It involved 3 pillars tenants, land and housing types, product, supply chain and platform, change management and housing delivery. The first phase concluded in June 2025 and informed the development of the strategy and implementation plan to embed MMC into housing delivery. Phase 2 – Implementation and refinement Phase 2 will build on the learnings, outcomes and recommendations from Phase 1 with a greater focus on “implementation and refinement”. It involves product and market development, supporting infrastructure and implementation support to measure and evaluate the success of the program.

An Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offers diverse support, including counselling, legal aid, and coaching, available through various formats like virtual and in-person sessions. Effective interventions are reported to show increased engagement and reduced turnover or burnout. Support is provided for traumatic incidents through best practice frameworks, with optional onsite support to help manage incidents and reduce harm. Reporting on these responses shows the benefits of regular support and assists managers in handling situations effectively.

contracts.title: NETM Evaluation Survey Provider
contracts.supplier: The Social Research Centre Pty Ltd
contracts.scope: The NETM program will comprise the development and delivery of 100 micro-credentials over a four-year piloting period, with an expected target of 25 in the first year. Industry partners will co-design and co-deliver micro-credentials to ensure training is relevant and meets industry skills demands in the priority industries of the Western Parkland City. NETM Education and Training Providers with proven capacity and capability to deliver innovative, high-quality learning will be contracted to deliver NETM micro-credentials in collaboration with industry partners. To assess the efficacy and outcomes achieved by the NETM pilot, the Authority will be implementing an evaluation framework that sets out the source of outcomes metrics, evaluation instruments and data processes for NETM evaluation and reporting over the life of the pilot. Surveys of learners, employers, industry partners and education providers will be a key source of evaluation data to assess individual micro-credentials as well as the NETM process overall. See the NETM Evaluation framework at Attachment A. The Authority seeks to secure an expert survey provider to design, review and deliver NETM evaluation surveys to ensure the accuracy and relevancy of data collected, maximise survey response rates and ensure survey design and delivery reflects industry best practice.

contracts.title: Local Sport Grant Program Evaluation
contracts.scope: The project will include the following: A review and confirmation of the current draft program logic and Evaluation Plan and update throughout the project as necessary. Conduct a detailed Post Evaluation of the 2022-23 and 2023-24 Programs process and outcomes, considering the design, planning, scheduling and resourcing of the program. Provide recommendations for future programs, specifically the 2025-26 Program. Ensuring that future programs are achieving the desired outcomes and increasing participation rates overall and among target populations and underrepresented groups. The program design needs to ensure that it has a geographical spread across NSW and is aligned to the Office of Sport 2024-2028 strategic plan. Conduct a detailed Formative Evaluation of the 2025-26 Program process and outcomes, considering the design, planning, scheduling and resourcing of the program. Manage stakeholder relations with parties who are participating in the evaluation. Issues management - Identify how to resolve issues that arise. Actively manage the project including reporting to the Office regularly on progress. Prepare draft, interim and final reports of all deliverables and brief the Office on potential findings throughout. Make specific recommendations regarding how the evaluation findings could be used to inform the design, implementation, and operation of the Program or other similar NSW Government grant programs, for example through gaps in the program or evaluation design and data collection. 2.10 Make specific recommendations about future design, assessment and other strategies or initiatives the Office could consider, to increase the engagement and participation of underrepresented groups including women and girls, people from culturally and linguistically diverse communities, people with disability, First Nations peoples and LGBTQIA+ people the sport and recreation sector.

contracts.title: CWS00161-1_Protecting breeding habitat of the superb parrot
contracts.scope: The proposed procurement activity is to provide a contract to Greening Australia to provide protection and restoration of superb parrot habitat in the NSW Riverina, South West Slopes and Southern Tablelands. The contract will be for a 4-year term (with no extension options), with a contract value of $523,628 excl GST, paid over the first two years of the contract. Funding is provided by the NSW Biodiversity Conservation Trust (BCT), via the NSW Saving Our Species (SoS) program and attached to WBS account EX-6882-T20103. The scope of the procurement includes the delivery of: 1. restoration of 250 hectares of superb parrot habitat using methods including direct seeding and tubestock planting of a mix of appropriate tree, shrub and ground cover plants. 2. monitoring of restoration success and plant survival rates in Year 3 and 4. 3. four landholder engagement events to achieve the restoration target.

contracts.title: Uperoleia mahonyi Conservation project
contracts.scope: This project aims to create a step-change in our capacity to enhance conservation outcomes for threatened species by assessing a suite of genomic tools that could provide managers with the critical information needed to rapidly decide on appropriate management actions. This project expects to bridge the gap between basic research and application by developing and applying new genomic tools to a real-world conservation case study. Expected outcomes include a framework for future integration of genomic approaches in adaptive conservation management. This should provide significant benefits, including increased accessibility to genomic tools that can rapidly provide the critical information needed to make informed conservation decisions.

contracts.scope: Wetlands in the Northern Tablelands region will be prioritised to increase the area of protected and enhanced wetlands on private and public property. Priority wetland sites (Upland Wetlands, Fens and Bogs) will be identified and mapped. Baseline floristic surveys will be conducted to establish baseline data for follow up monitoring to measure changes in floristic biodiversity, particularly within wetland areas that have undergone changes in land management activities. The project will increase awareness in land managers and the wider community on the significance of wetlands via site visits and facilitated workshops. Skills and Knowledge surveys will measure land managers capacity to change land management practices.

contracts.title: Sleep and Rest Safe Sleep training for Centre based and FDC services
contracts.scope: Deliverables Description Detailed project plan The detailed project plan should include information such as key timings and milestones, risks and mitigation, review and feedback of draft content by the Department, evaluation process and preparation of the final data report. This can be discussed during the inception meeting. Redevelopment of the Existing Course and receipt of the Modified Training Course The Department seeks engaging and practical sector resources accessible to targeted educators and staff, that provide key regulatory quality and safety information and guidance. The Department welcomes innovative ideas Red Nose might have about engaging language, content and interactivity. Any additional content and included materials are to be sourced from reputable sources, expert industry specialists and/or accredited by a relevant sector expert such as NSW government departments or ACECQA. The purpose of the redevelopment is to bring the Existing Course in line with the October sleep regulation changes (84A-D) to create the Modified Training Course. The Department is to provide Red Nose with an extracted version of the Existing Course, with suggested changes as a starting point for amendments. This will consider any video content that contains names, logos or any identifying imagery of current services or providers being removed. Any key information included in the video to be included in another manner, such as text based interactive content or other. Red Nose will develop the Modified Training Course to be hosted on Red Noses LMS platform. As part of the existing format of the nine modules, the following concepts must be included: 1. Division 1A Sleep regulation changes (October 2023); 2. Supervision - sleeping/resting children always being in sight and hearing distance of an educator; 3. Supervision - physical checks of sleeping/resting children; 4. Safe equipment; 5. Safe environment; and 6. Effective risk assessments, policies and procedures for safe sleep. The completion certificate is to be amended to include the completion date and distinguish between Red Nose's Existing Course and the Department's funded enrolments into the Modified Training Course. Red Nose must provide draft content to the Departments project team for review and feedback. Red Nose must work with the project team to address feedback and suggested amendments and allow adequate time for this to occur. contracts.title: WPCA000177 - Stormwater Trunk Infrastructure Design
contracts.scope: Project Overview The WPCA is tasked with the design and delivery of the Bradfield City Centre – creating a dynamic new place for people to live, work and learn. The Bradfield City Centre comprises a total land area of 114.9ha of land located at 215 Badgery’s Creek Road. The first phase of creation involves the delivery of approximately 20 hectares in the western portion of the site. Concurrent Engagements As part of the first phase of City creation, several concurrent activities are occurring involving a number of consultants that have been engaged or are in the process of being engaged. The main engagement that the Sewer Pump Station and Stormwater Infrastructure Consultant will interface with is the First Stage Enabling Works Head Consultant. The First Stage Enabling Works Head Consultant will provide the following services: • Civil Works: Site gradings, earthworks, road pavements, piped and open stormwater drainage and coordination with streetscape landscaping. • Water Utilities: Potable and recycled water reticulation mains, and stormwater network for non-potable water uses. • Digital Smart City: Providing for all the digital plumbing including pits and pipes, smart poles and connections to the future communication data centres • Electrical Utilities: Providing for all the electrical reticulation network to service the wider precincts with Bradfield City Centre. • Waste: Design of a dedicated organic food collection pressure pipe system and collection tank for all the organic food waste to enable waste to energy opportunities. The collection tank will connect to the sewer pump station for overflow discharge. Services under this Engagement The following design work and construction phase services are envisaged to be managed and delivered by the consultant: • Stormwater Design: detailed modelling for all aspects of precinct wide stormwater quality and quantity to allow the concept design of the stormwater management strategy infrastructure for the entire Bradfield City Centre. Detailed design of Parkland West aspects of the stormwater infrastructure along Moore Gully. Detailed design of Parkland East aspects of the stormwater infrastructure along Thompson Creek. • Technical Advice: provision of technical advice and design solutions for options (allow consideration of 2 options) for servicing Bradfield City Centre’s recycled water demand from utilising on-site stormwater.

contracts.agency: NSW Department of Communities and Justice
contracts.title: Aboriginal Led Commissioning
contracts.supplier: AbSec - NSW Child, Family and Community Peak Aboriginal Corporation
contracts.scope: The NSW Government is funding the ALC initiative under the Closing the Gap (CTG) Priority Reforms that are set out in the NSW Closing the Gap Implementation Plan 2022-2024. The objective of Aboriginal-led commissioning is to drive an approach to commissioning that gives Aboriginal communities decision making power when it comes to the design, delivery and monitoring of programs and services, and ensures that they: build on the strengths of communities are culturally embedded, and are responsive to opportunities and needs that communities identify themselves. Driven by principles of self-determination and accountability, the ALC initiative will ensure that solutions are owned by Aboriginal communities and place Aboriginal culture as a key driver in service design. The ALC initiative aims to deliver outcomes for Aboriginal people and communities that are defined and driven by Aboriginal people and communities. The ALC initiative will be led by an Aboriginal Controlled Community Organisation (ACC), that will design and trial an approach to Aboriginal-led commissioning over two phases: Phase 1: establish a project team to carry out strategy, design and planning for implementation of a model for Aboriginal-led commissioning. Phase 2: trial the implementation of the model by commissioning service delivery initiatives in trial sites identified in partnership with a cross-agency steering committee.

contracts.title: Powerhouse Ultimo Renewal - Mechanical & Electrical Services
contracts.scope: The Powerhouse Ultimo Renewal (PUR) project vision is to see Powerhouse Ultimo focus on design and fashion, presenting exhibitions that showcase the museums significant collections, international exclusive exhibitions and programs that support the design and fashion industries. The renewal will deliver expanded and refurbished exhibition and public space, connecting Powerhouse Ultimo to the Sydney CBD by re-orienting the museum to the Goods Line and adjacent dining, entertaining and cultural precincts. A significant investment in the development of a creative industries precinct will deliver subsidised studio and workspaces at Ultimo, resulting in a vibrant precinct. A design competition is currently underway, led by Create NSW, with the successful scheme to be awarded in December 2022. The PUR project is being delivered by Infrastructure NSW on behalf of Powerhouse and Create. The delivery includes completion of a Stage 2 State Significant Development Application (SSDA) along with the preparation of tender documentation for a contractor to construct the project. This request is to engage a mechanical and electrical services provider to support the development of the PUR project. The delivery includes completion of the following stages of the project: Development of Concept Design; Schematic Design; SSDA documentation; Design Development; Tender Documentation; Contractor Procurement; Design Development Completion; Construction Documentation; Construction Phase Services; and Defect Liability Period Services.

contracts.agency: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development
contracts.title: NSW Aquaculture Economic Contributions Study
contracts.scope: The aim of this study is to estimate the economic contribution of aquaculture activity in NSW in 2021/22 with optional update analyses undertaken for the 2023/24, 2025/26 and 2027/28 financial years. As a result of the need for industry to justify sector status for event recovery responses, the contributions of these sectors will be based on a local government area and estuary region basis. The economic contribution of each sector will also be presented at a state level. The study will focus on primary production but will also quantify the economic contribution along the seafood supply-chain to the extent possible within the proposed approach. A three-year forecast for each sector will be developed from primary data, relevant reports and interviews with key industry representatives.

The contract will ensure that appropriate staff are correctly attired to perform their duties safely and professionally. The joint venture allows the cluster to achieve a collective bargaining power and to seek competitive pricing and a high quality uniform. It allows for innovations in procurement systems, improved auditing and access to new designs and improvements in apparel. The contract will be awarded for an initial 5 years with a 3 year extension for a total of 8 years. The Cluster went to market in 2018 and negotiations were undertaken in 2019 with the preferred supplier prior to awarding.

Its structure will support Government Agencies by ensuring matters are outsourced to Law Firms with the right expertise to achieve positive outcomes that represent value for money. The Panel is comprised of the following seven Primary Streams for General Lines: medical negligence; oabuse; intentional torts / protective actions; personal injury (not including workers compensation); employment; recovery and other general claims.
